newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso keeps re-election plans on track.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso keeps re-election plans on track.

text.p: President Fernando Henrique Cardoso appeared to have kept on track his plans for a second term on Monday after Brazil's biggest party agreed to vote this week on a bill allowing his re-election, a spokesman said.

Senior officials from the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB) told Cardoso they would vote on the re-election issue on Tuesday, despite a decision at a party convention on Sunday to delay voting on it until Feb. 15, presidential spokesman Sergio Amaral said.
"There was agreement that the motion voted yesterday was a recommendation and that it should not upset the timetable for voting on re-election," Amaral told reporters.
But PMDB deputies and senators, who were summoned by Cardoso to explain the party's position, left the presidential palace without confirming the agreement and were reported to be locked in meetings.

The PMDB did not support Cardoso's victorious presidential campaign in 1994 but has generally voted in line with his administration and has three ministers in the cabinet. But the president's plan to rewrite the constitution and stand for a second term in 1998 has split the party between those in favour and those against the government.
"The PMDB cannot be in the government and behave as if it were in the opposition," Amaral said, refering to Sunday's decision to delay voting on the issue.

Government leaders intend to put a controversial constitutional amendment, allowing re-election for presidents, state governors and mayors, to a first vote in a Chamber of Deputies committee on Tuesday. The bill, which faces a long journey through Congress, would undo a founding tenet of the Brazilian republic, founded in 1889, which has always banned re-election for holders of executive office.
